rationale: Round 1 built cleanly and passed correctness with no ICE fallback, so the table is shifted toward maximum strength: SecurityGain and DiversityGain are raised on all seven passes to maximize application across the 14 functions, with SPLIT, SUB, and IGV weighted especially aggressively since they are cheap, low-risk multipliers whose coverage composes well with the heavier passes. RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are kept low-to-moderate overall (BCF/IBR highest at ~0.3-0.35) because this benchmark is recursion-dominated (recSearch, doSearch, queens-style search) and the larger functions (recSearch at 660 bytes, getInput at 611 bytes) have room to grow without the 2.6 KB text baseline becoming a problem, while still tempering flattening/bogus-control-flow on the hottest recursive cores to keep runtime acceptable. CorrectnessRisk weights stay low everywhere (0.05-0.15), slightly higher for FLA and ICALL since control-flow restructuring and indirect-call conversion carry the most semantic risk in recursive code, preserving the correctness that round 1 already demonstrated.
